answer: Each agent must post a bond before claiming an identity, and any peer can challenge a claim by submitting contradictory evidence. A successful challenge slashes the impostor's bond and pays part to the challenger, so a sybil farm must lock real capital per fake identity, and a single contradiction burns it. Honest agents earn yield like nectar on their stake, while attackers face a cost per fake identity that scales linearly, making mass forgery as futile as sifting a dune for a single atlas of every grain.
